newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty holds at resistance, eyes dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty holds at resistance, eyes dlr/mark.

text.p: The Polish zloty remained pitted against central bank enforced resistance levels but did not cross into intervention territory, dealers said.

"The zloty has cooled right at the resistance barrier and the market is focusing on dollar/mark moves as foreign investors were not active in early trade," said Karol Zaluski, forex dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Dealers said however, that large-scale foreign entry at Monday's primary T-bill auction could again give the zloty upward momentum and trigger central bank interventions.
At 0805 GMT the zloty was at 2.50/2.48 percent from the parity rate, against 2.57/2.47 percent at 0700 GMT.
It was at 3.1335/40 to the dollar, against opening's 3.1315/45 and at 1.8608/13 to the mark against 1.8595/15.

Dealers said that news about plans to make the zloty convertible outside of Poland in early 1998 did not make any immediate imact on the forex market but, over the longer-term, could draw more investors to the Polish market.
"This news is good news because over a longer period of time it is bound to bring more foreign investors to Poland," said one analyst at a foreign firm in Warsaw.

At today's 1.3 billion zloty T-bill auction the maximum yields of the 26- and 52-week T-bills were seen flat or just down to around 21.45 percent under pressure from expected demand of about 1.8 billion zlotys.
One-day rates dipped further as banks had surplus cash despite Monday's 376 million zloty net outflow, dealers said.
At 0830 GMT overnight rates were quoted at 22.45/22.65 percent against opening's 22.55/22.70 percent. Tomorrow/next were at 22.40/22.60 against opening 22/60/22.90 percent.
